\ln(x) = 0.06 t + c_1
\]
\[
x = \exp(0.06 t + c_1)
\]\[
x = \exp(0.06 t) * \exp(c_1)
\]\[
x = c * \exp(0.06 t)

heading: 2.3 Chaotic behaviour: Lorenz Attractor
text: Lorenz equations first chaotic system discovered. three differential equations derived represent idealized behavior earth’s atmosphere:\(\frac{dx}{dt} = -\frac{8}{3}x+yz\)\(\frac{dy}{dt} = -10 (y - z)\)\(\frac{dz}{dt} = -xy + 28y-z\)Run code visualize Lorenz AttractorRecord last \(x\), \(y\), \(z\) values using tail()Quiz Question 10: Apply small change initial conditions rerun code. changes affect final \(x\), \(y\), \(z\) values?
code:
Lorenz <- function(t, state, parameters)
{
  with(as.list(c(state)), {
    dx <- -8 / 3 * x + y * z
    dy <- -10 * (y - z)
    dz <- -x * y + 28 * y - z

granger.fun <- function(x) {
  n <- length(x)
  # Get first (a) and second (b) variable
  a <- x[1:(n/2)]
  b <- x[(n/2+1):n]
  # Convert to time series
  a <- ts(a)
  b <- ts(b)
  tsDat <- ts.union(a, b)
  tsVAR <- vars::VAR(tsDat, p = 12)
  # Apply Granger causality test

detrend.anomalies.fun <- function(dates, values) {
  df <- data.frame(dates, values)
  
  # (1) Anomalies
  # Extract day and month to identify each day of the year
  df$day_of_year <- format(df$dates, "%m-%d")
  
  # Calculate the mean for each day of the year across all years
  daily_means <- aggregate(values ~ day_of_year,
                           data = df,
                           FUN = mean,
                           na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Merge the daily means back to the original data to calculate anomalies
  df <- merge(df,
              daily_means,
              by = "day_of_year",
              suffixes = c("", "_mean"))
  
  # Calculate anomalies by subtracting the daily mean from each value
  df$anomaly <- df$values - df$values_mean
  
  # Sort by date
  df <- df[order(df$date), ]
  
  # (2) Detrend
  time <- 1:length(dates)
  linear.trend <- lm(formula = df$anomaly ~ time, na.action = na.exclude)
  detr.anom <- residuals(linear.trend)
  result <- ts(detr.anom)
  return(result)
}

grangerPvaluesLags.fun <- function(x, y) {
  tsDat <- ts.union(x, y)
  # Set the maximum lag to test
  max_lag <- 14
  p_values <- numeric(max_lag)
  
  # Loop over each lag and calculate the Granger causality p-value

    causality_result <- causality(tsVAR, cause = "x")
    p_values[lag] <- causality_result$Granger$p.value
  }
  return(ts(p_values))
